title: Becoming an HVAC Technician in Texas
desc: Are you interested in starting your career as an HVAC technician? Learn more about what it takes on our newest blog post!

blocks.text: Are you interested in starting your career as an HVAC technician? Like other professions, becoming an HVAC technician takes time and requires formal training and certifications. Not every technician follows the same career trajectory with many people varying in when they start their training and when they finish. Here’s what you need to know about becoming an HVAC technician in Texas.

For maximum exposure to the HVAC industry, you should begin your professional journey in high school. Study hard in your math and physics courses. Vocational classes that give you preliminary knowledge of plumbing and electricity will also help your future career. The state of Texas requires a high school diploma or GED to become a technician. This formal degree will also increase your wage and job opportunities in the future.

After graduating high school, complete an HVAC program at a local trade school. Technical training, as well as courses on refrigeration, can widen your skillset and improve your understanding of commercial and residential systems. Trade schools will also allow you to experience hands-on training. These courses can take up to two years to complete depending on your field of study.
Many employers prefer technicians with additional certifications and expertise. Adding experience to your resume will ease your job search and give you access to more elite workplaces.

During your formal education, ensure you’re getting the right certifications. If you plan to work with air conditioners and refrigerants, for example, you’ll require a Section 608 Technician Certification from the Environmental Protection Agency. Becoming EPA-certified is a huge plus in the job market. This certification requires you to take and pass several core tests through an EPA-approved certifying organization.

Once you have the preliminary EPA certification, you can polish up your resume and begin applying for jobs. Network locally to find HVAC companies or search online job boards for positions. Going through a trade school often gives you a lot of opportunities to find other professionals in the field. You could even have a job lined up for you once you complete your courses.

To further your education, you need to find a position working under a licensed HVAC contractor. Once you secure a position, you can fill out a technician application for the Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation. This application comes with a nonrefundable $20 fee and is open to anyone above the age of 18. It’s important to note that registrations with this organization are valid for one year after the issue date.

Once your registration is approved, you’re officially an HVAC technician. You can continue to provide heating, cooling and refrigeration services to residents and businesses. Many technicians begin by cleaning furnaces and providing other basic maintenance and repairs. As you gain experience, you’ll have more opportunities to do harder tasks like installing new systems and soldering pipes. You’ll also have to consider expanding your formal education in the future.

Individual HVAC companies may have different requirements for their technicians. The HVAC industry is constantly evolving as new technology and advancements are released. To stay up-to-date in the field, it’s your responsibility to continue to take formal classes. You need specific certifications to be able to do electrical services or pipework. Improving your education gives you access to more challenging work.

Once you’re a registered HVAC technician in Texas, you can also work on becoming NATE-certified. The North American Technician Excellence organization is a distinguished nonprofit known for its industry excellence. Many employers prefer those with a NATE certification as it shows your expertise and experience in the field. To become NATE-certified, you have to register for a NATE program and pass the exams. You could receive a basic NATE certification with as little as one year of experience.
Anyone can become a registered HVAC technician with the right training and education. Start your exciting new career journey as a heating and cooling expert today.
